answer: Reputation staking resists sybil attacks by making each identity earn trust slowly. A new agent enters cold as a glacier, with near-zero weight; its attestations count only after peers vouch over time. To fake a velvet-smooth crowd of trusted agents, an attacker must farm reputation on every fake account for weeks, paying compute and stake on each. Burn one for fraud and it is slashed, so the cost scales per identity like planting a whole cedar forest, not one seed.
